wxdragon-sys 0.9.22 (crates.io, MIT OR Apache-2.0), vendored for BrailleCraft.

Changes, all in cpp/include/core/wxd_print.h and cpp/src/print.cpp, marked "Added for BrailleCraft":
- wxd_FontEnumerator_GetFacenames: the system's font face names (wxFontEnumerator), one per line.
- wxd_PrintData_Assign: copy one print data object into another.
- wxd_PrintData_SetPrinterName / wxd_PrintData_GetPrinterName: the chosen printer.
- wxd_PrintData_SetPaperSizeTenthsMM / wxd_PrintData_GetPaperSizeTenthsMM: the paper, by its size (a standard
  paper when one has that size, else a custom size).
- wxd_PrintData_SetLandscape / wxd_PrintData_IsLandscape: the orientation.
- wxd_PrintData_SetNoCopies: the copy count.
- wxd_Printer_GetLastError: whether the last print was cancelled or failed.
- wxd_Printout_GetPaperRectPixels: the paper's rectangle in printer pixels, so margins are measured from the paper's
  edge.

Also added, in cpp/include/core/wxd_reader_static_text.h and cpp/src/reader_static_text.cpp (listed in
cpp/CMakeLists.txt and included from cpp/include/wxdragon.h):
- WxdReaderStaticText: a wxStaticText that accepts focus, and so is reached by Tab, on Windows while the system's
  screen reader flag (SPI_GETSCREENREADER) is on and the text is not empty; dialog resources name it with
  subclass="WxdReaderStaticText".
- wxd_ReaderStaticText_Registered: whether that class is registered; called once at start-up so the class is kept.

Also added, in cpp/include/core/wxd_cursor_locator.h and cpp/src/cursor_locator.cpp (listed in cpp/CMakeLists.txt
and included from cpp/include/wxdragon.h):
- wxd_TextCtrl_ShowCursorLocator: the Cursor Locator over a multi-line text control, a rectangle closing in on the
  caret, drawn with four borderless popup windows in the window text colour.

Also added, in cpp/include/core/wxd_space_after.h, cpp/src/space_after.cpp and cpp/src/space_after_osx.mm
(macOS only; listed in cpp/CMakeLists.txt and included from cpp/include/wxdragon.h):
- wxd_TextCtrl_SetSpaceAfter: empty space after a line of a multi-line text control, with no text in it: the
  text view's pixels-below-lines tag on GTK, its paragraph spacing on macOS, wxWidgets' paragraph spacing on
  Windows.
  cpp/CMakeLists.txt adds the GTK 3 include directories (pkg-config gtk+-3.0) on Linux for it.

Also added, in cpp/include/core/wxd_line_gutter.h and cpp/src/line_gutter.cpp (listed in cpp/CMakeLists.txt and
included from cpp/include/wxdragon.h):
- wxd_LineGutter_Create and wxd_LineGutter_SetMarks: a narrow drawn column beside a multi-line text control showing
  labels (line numbers) at the height of given text positions, repainted when the control scrolls or is resized.

Also added, in cpp/include/core/wxd_doc_editor.h, cpp/src/doc_editor.cpp, cpp/src/doc_editor_internal.h,
cpp/src/doc_editor_gtk.cpp (Linux), cpp/src/doc_editor_msw.cpp (Windows) and cpp/src/doc_editor_osx.mm (macOS; all
listed in cpp/CMakeLists.txt and the header included from cpp/include/wxdragon.h):
- wxd_DocEditor_Create and the other wxd_DocEditor_ functions: the document editing window, drawn by the program (a
  wxScrolledCanvas): rows of text and page break rows (a line across), the selection, the system caret, a line
  number column, the Cursor Locator drawn in the window; keys, typed characters (and keys let go), clicks and focus
  handed to the program through callbacks; one row per wheel notch; the scroll box takes effect when let go.
- Its text for screen readers: on Linux an ATK object with the text interface given out through the widget class's
  get_accessible; on Windows a UI Automation provider (element, Text pattern, text ranges) answering WM_GETOBJECT,
  with UiaReturnRawElementProvider and the text changed and selection changed events, while
  wxd_DocEditor_SetSupportUIAutomation is on; on macOS the accessibility text area methods added to the window's view
  by a subclass made at run time, with the value changed and selected text changed notifications.
- build.rs links uiautomationcore on Windows for it.
- The window keeps no row text (plan line L1, large documents): wxd_DocEditor_SetRows gives it the count of rows,
  each row's kind and length and the longest length; the window asks the program for a row's text through the row
  function given to wxd_DocEditor_Create (as drawn, for screen readers, or its line number label) as it draws,
  measures or reads it, and holds at most 1024 rows; wxd_DocEditor_SetCaret carries the caret row's text, since the
  program cannot answer while it places the caret; the text screen readers get is put together by parts from the
  rows, never held whole; the stretch that changed (offset, removed and inserted text) comes with SetRows for the
  ATK text-remove and text-insert signals.
- On Windows the window is created under a class of its own, "BrailleCraftEditor" (wxApp::GetRegisteredClassName and
  CreateUsingMSWClass), with the control id 0, so screen reader scripts can tell the editing area from every other
  window by its class.
- A click's column (DocEditor::ClickColumn): the caret goes before the first character whose left edge is right of
  the click less half a character width (spec 27 section 9, unknown 4); ColumnAt stays for the accessible text's
  point-to-place.
- wxd_App_HandlePendingEvents: wxApp::Yield, for the embossing progress window that stays open, its Cancel button
  live, while the job is sent.
- wxd_DocEditor_GetRawKey: the physical key of the key event being handed to the program (the scan code on Windows,
  the hardware key code less 8 on Linux, the virtual key code on macOS), for six-key entry, which names keys by
  their place on the keyboard.
- wxd_ListBox_IsSelected (cpp/include/widgets/wxd_listbox.h, cpp/src/listbox.cpp): whether an item of a list box
  that takes several choices is chosen, for the start-up embosser autoprobe's printer list.

The Rust bindings are generated from the header when the crate builds, so no Rust file changed.
The workspace Cargo.toml uses this copy through [patch.crates-io].

Also added, in cpp/include/core/wxd_save_dialog.h and cpp/src/save_dialog.cpp (listed in cpp/CMakeLists.txt and
included from cpp/include/wxdragon.h):
- wxd_SaveDialog_WithChoice: a Save As file dialog with a labelled choice in it (through wxFileDialogCustomizeHook),
  shown only for given file types; on Linux the GTK file chooser's "filter" property is watched to follow the type,
  and the panel holding the controls is fitted to them again when they are shown or hidden.

Also added, in cpp/include/core/wxd_screenshot.h and cpp/src/screenshot.cpp (listed in cpp/CMakeLists.txt and
included from cpp/include/wxdragon.h):
- wxd_App_SaveScreenshot: a picture of every shown top-level window of the program, read back from the screen
  (wxScreenDC) as one PNG file, for the control channel's screenshot tool (braillecraft-cli mcp --connect).

Also added, in cpp/include/core/wxd_doc_tabs.h and cpp/src/doc_tabs.cpp (listed in cpp/CMakeLists.txt and included
from cpp/include/wxdragon.h):
- wxd_DocTabs_Create and the other wxd_DocTabs_ functions: the tab bar of the main window, a wxNotebook with one
  tab per open document and the behaviour of a browser's tab bar: a close button in each tab (a real GTK button
  packed into the tab's label box on Linux; the tab's image, hit-tested by the tab control, on Windows), a middle
  click to close, tabs dragged to reorder (GTK's own reorderable tabs, put back and redone through the toolkit's
  remove and insert so its page list stays in step; a drag across the tab row elsewhere), the keys Ctrl+Tab,
  Ctrl+Shift+Tab, Ctrl+W and Ctrl+Shift+Page Up and Page Down while the tab bar has the focus, and callbacks to the
  program for a selection change, a close request and a move; TabRect and CloseButtonRect give the screen
  rectangles for a program that drives the window (the control channel).
- On Windows the tabs are drawn by the program (TCS_OWNERDRAWFIXED through an MSWGetStyle override, so DocTabs is
  made with wxNotebook's default constructor and Create; the inside of each tab through MSWOnDraw, and in dark mode
  the whole control through a paint handler, since wxNotebook then paints everything itself): the name, then the
  close sign at the right of the text (a blank image of the sign's size keeps the room for it), with a hover and a
  pressed background, closed when the click is let go on it; system colours, the highlight colours in high
  contrast; padding and the image follow the DPI. A context menu on a tab (right button, Shift+F10, the
  Applications key): Close Tab, Move Tab Left, Move Tab Right. CloseButtonRect gives the sign at the right.
  wxd_DocTabs_ShowFocus puts the focus on the tab bar with the keyboard cues on (for the build checks' picture).

Also added, in cpp/include/core/wxd_window_tabs.h, cpp/src/window_tabs_osx.mm (macOS only) and
cpp/src/window_tabs.cpp (the other systems, where each function does nothing; both listed in cpp/CMakeLists.txt and
the header included from cpp/include/wxdragon.h):
- wxd_WindowTabs_Enable: window tabbing on for the program (wxApp::OSXEnableAutomaticTabbing, which wxWidgets turns
  off at launch), the program's own AppleWindowTabbingMode default "manual" so its other windows are not tabbed, the
  program frame never tabbed and its menu bar kept as the common menu bar (wxMenuBar::MacSetCommonMenuBar).
- wxd_WindowTabs_Prepare: a document window, its tabbing identifier shared by the document windows, and the plus
  button of its tab bar (newWindowForTab:, added to wxWidgets' window class at run time with class_addMethod,
  calling back the program for the window it was given to and doing nothing for any other window).
- wxd_WindowTabs_Add (the window as the last tab of another's tab group, addTabbedWindow:ordered:),
  wxd_WindowTabs_ShowTabBar, wxd_WindowTabs_Select, wxd_WindowTabs_Step (selectNextTab: and selectPreviousTab:),
  wxd_WindowTabs_Move (the tab to another place in its group), wxd_WindowTabs_GroupOrder (a group's windows in tab
  order), wxd_WindowTabs_SetEdited (wxTopLevelWindow::OSXSetModified), wxd_WindowTabs_IsKey, and
  wxd_WindowTabs_MenuDump (every main menu item, for the build checks).
